title: Heartbeat-checkpoint integration with parallel executor
description:
## Goal

Integrate heartbeat-and-per-SNR-boundary checkpointing with the
parallel executor: SIGINT mid-run flushes a checkpoint with the
per-worker state from design-doc §4 schema v2; `--resume` from that
checkpoint produces byte-identical deterministic columns vs an
uninterrupted reference run at the same seed.

## Context

Task under story `bcf7776d` (CPU foundation) within epic `gf2-sim`
(`f9717e7e`). Phase 0 design doc:
`dev/active/ec530af9-pipeline-design.md` §4 (heartbeat schema v2),
§3 (per-worker seek scheme). Sequencing:
- depends on `3fcb7025` (per-worker dispatch must exist)
- depends on `db9836e4` (channels must exist so heartbeat tests
  exercise the AWGN + Rayleigh paths — adds the edge per audit C5)

## AMENDMENT 2026-06-08 (user-approved): v2-only schema, offline v1 migration

This task body originally specified an in-reader v1/v2 back-compat
`CheckpointReader` (load a legacy `SimulationRunner` v1 checkpoint
directly) — which **contradicts the user-approved design doc §4 (Q5,
2026-06-07)**: the new pipeline is **v2-only**; there is **no in-reader
v1 back-compat**; legacy v1 checkpoints are converted **offline** by a
one-shot migration binary `crates/gf2-sim/src/bin/checkpoint_migrate.rs`
(§4 "Migration tool"). The epic's Q5 row records the same decision
("v2-only checkpoint schema; one-shot migration tool for v1"). The
design doc is the SSOT, so the deliverables and criteria below are
amended to match it. **No correctness criterion is relaxed**: the v1
data path is still exercised end-to-end (migrate → load → resume →
byte-identical), just via the offline tool instead of the reader.

## Deliverables

1. `crates/gf2-sim/src/checkpoint/mod.rs` containing:
   - `pub struct CheckpointWriter` that serialises per-SNR state to
     `<dir>/snr_<NNNN>.json` per design-doc §4 schema v2
     (`worker_states[]` required, `schema_version: 2`, `config_hash`
     blake3 of serialised `PipelineConfig`).
   - `pub struct CheckpointReader` that loads **v2 only** and restores
     per-worker `rng_word_pos`. A non-v2 `schema_version` (or a
     `config_hash` mismatch vs the live config) is a hard load error
     (`FatalError::ConfigHashMismatch` per §4), NOT a silent v1 path.
   - Atomic write: write to `.tmp`, fsync, rename.
2. Integration with the parallel executor (`gf2-sim::parallel`):
   - Hooks at SNR boundary (always flush) and at heartbeat interval
     (`heartbeat_every_frames` from `PipelineConfig`).
   - SIGINT handler installed via `ctrlc` crate; on signal:
     - Stop accepting new batches.
     - Wait for in-flight workers to settle on a frame boundary
       (drain commit contract, §4).
     - Flush checkpoint, fsync, exit non-zero.
3. One-shot v1→v2 migration binary
   `crates/gf2-sim/src/bin/checkpoint_migrate.rs` per design-doc §4
   "Migration tool":
   - CLI `checkpoint_migrate --input <v1-dir> --output <v2-dir>
     [--parallelism N]`.
   - Reads each `<v1-dir>/snr_NNNN.json`, synthesises a single-worker
     v2 checkpoint (`worker_states[0].frames_in_worker =
     frames_completed`, `worker_states[0].rng_word_pos = rng_word_pos`),
     writes `<v2-dir>/snr_NNNN.json`.
   - Tested against the 2026-06-05 checkpoint dir at
     `dev/benchmarks/dvb_t2_awgn/curve_1_2_16qam/checkpoints/`.
4. Tests in `tests/checkpoint_compat.rs`:
   - v1→v2 migration: a checkpoint produced by the legacy
     `gf2_coding::simulation::SimulationRunner` is migrated by the
     tool, then the resulting **v2** checkpoint loads and resumes on
     the single-worker path with byte-identical results vs the
     uninterrupted single-thread reference.
   - v2 round-trip: a v2 checkpoint loads, resumes on the N-worker
     path, byte-identical `fer / frames / errors / mean_iters` vs an
     uninterrupted N-worker reference run.
5. Cross-channel coverage tests:
   - Resume tests run on at least one Rayleigh and one Rician
     configuration as well as AWGN, so the heartbeat path is
     exercised across the fading stages (per audit finding C5).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] SIGINT mid-run on a 10-SNR sweep flushes a v2 checkpoint
  per the design-doc §4 schema; re-invoking with `--resume`
  produces byte-identical `fer / frames / errors / mean_iters`
  vs an uninterrupted reference run at the same seed across all
  three channel types (AWGN, Rayleigh, Rician).
- [hard] v1 migration compat: a checkpoint produced by the legacy
  `gf2_coding::simulation::SimulationRunner` is converted by
  `checkpoint_migrate` to a v2 checkpoint, which then loads and
  resumes on the single-worker path with byte-identical results vs
  the uninterrupted single-thread reference. (The reader itself is
  v2-only per §4; v1 support is the offline tool, not the reader.)
- [hard] Atomic write: a test that kills the writer mid-flush (via
  signal during fsync) leaves either a complete previous-state
  checkpoint or no new file at all; never a partial JSON.
- [hard] `cargo-ci`, `code-review` gates green.

## Non-goals

- GPU-pipeline drain semantics (owned by Phase C `571c11c4`).
- Across-SNR parallelism checkpointing (epic non-goal — within-SNR
  parallelism is the contract; cross-SNR parallel was the legacy
  `run_coded_iterative_parallel` path that is not migrated).
- In-reader v1 back-compat (design doc §4 is v2-only; v1 is handled
  by the offline `checkpoint_migrate` tool, deliverable 3).
